title: Zoom In: An Introduction to Circuits
excerpt: Chris Olah, Nick Cammarata, Ludwig Schubert, and Gabriel Goh introduce the circuits research program with zoomable multiscale representations that link neurons, features, and model behavior in vision networks. The framing remains foundational for mechanistic interpretability even as the field shifts toward language models.
author: Chris Olah et al.

title: Activation Atlas
excerpt: Chris Olah, Arvind Satyanarayan, James Wexler, Ian Johnson, and collaborators aggregate millions of activations into navigable atlases that reveal how vision models organize concepts spatially. The technique is CNN-centric and does not directly transfer to transformer hidden states without substantial adaptation.
author: Chris Olah et al.

title: The Illustrated BERT, ELMo, and co. (How NLP Cracked Transfer Learning in NLP)
excerpt: Jay Alammar explains BERT, ELMo, and the pretrain-finetune paradigm with visual walkthroughs of tokenization, masking, and downstream heads. It predates decoder-only LLM dominance but remains the clearest introduction to bidirectional encoder transfer learning.
author: Jay Alammar
coverAlt: Jay Alammar illustrated NLP guide cover

title: AI and Efficiency
excerpt: Andrej Karpathy argues that algorithmic efficiency gains compound faster than Moore's law for deep learning, using ImageNet training cost curves as evidence that research progress shrinks compute budgets for fixed capability. The 2019 datapoints predate the LLM scaling era but the argument structure still informs efficiency debates.
author: Andrej Karpathy

title: Contrastive Representation Learning
excerpt: Lilian Weng surveys contrastive learning from instance discrimination through SimCLR, MoCo, and multimodal CLIP-style objectives, explaining why negative sampling, augmentations, and batch size matter. The post focuses on vision and early multimodal setups rather than latest LLM contrastive fine-tuning recipes.
author: Lilian Weng

title: Machine Learning Systems Design: 200+ Case Studies
excerpt: Eugene Yan collects over 200 public write-ups of ML systems design decisions—data pipelines, feature stores, monitoring, and deployment trade-offs—organized as searchable patterns rather than a single methodology. Entries vary in depth and recency; the catalog is descriptive, not a ranked benchmark.
author: Eugene Yan
